clue.text: 26 part 1's work moulded in turn

definitions.note: the first part of 26, Thomas, in the possessive: the Dylan Thomas piece

indicators.note: turn signals a reworking of the letters, as a lathe turns wood into a new shape

explanation.surface: Something made by the man of 26 has been shaped and moulded, perhaps on a potter's wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'turn', with 'in' as part of the fodder: WORK MOULDED IN has the letters of the play. 26 is THOMAS STEARNS, and its first part names the Welsh poet Dylan Thomas, who wrote this radio play.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas wrote this famous radio drama about a Welsh village, so it is the Thomas piece the clue points at.

clue.text: Recalling the past could be costing about a pound

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next pieces
could be says these letters might form something else once rearranged

parts.note: L, from the Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Thinking fondly of old prices, someone remembers when things cost about a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges COSTING into NOSTGIC, and 'about' puts it round A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wistful about bygone days is exactly what this adjective describes: a longing for the past.

clue.text: Poet and priest at his location

parts.note: Eli is the priest of Shiloh who raised Samuel in the Bible
Eli appears in the Old Testament, abbreviated OT, so that is where he is found

explanation.surface: A poet and a clergyman are seen together at the priest's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at his location' looks like his home or parish, but it is the part of the Bible where the priest Eli appears.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot, author of The Waste Land, is one of the best-known modern poets.

clue.text: Complaint about golden number by one from Yorkshire or Devon?

indicators.note: about says the complaint wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: a moan is a grumble or complaint
or is the heraldic word for gold
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

explanation.surface: A grumble about a golden number from someone living in Yorkshire or Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire and Devon both have great moors (the North York Moors, Dartmoor and Exmoor), hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives on or works the moorland is a moor-dweller, and these counties are famous for moors.

clue.text: As company is to 2?

parts.note: two's company in the proverb, and a ... company in Britain needs at least two officers, a director and a secretary

explanation.definitionFit: A British company with restricted liability is described by this word, as in Ltd after its name.

clue.text: 3's Cumbrian waterbuck?

parts.note: read with the water that follows, Wast Water is a lake in Cumbria in the English Lake District, giving its first part
the buck left after the water is an eland, a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An Eliot fan spots an antelope wading in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waterbuck' is a real antelope, but here the word splits: 'Cumbrian water' is Wast Water and 'buck' is an ELAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot's long 1922 poem has this title, so it is a work by the poet of 3.

clue.text: Plain green circle on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top places the circle above the next piece

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A plain green circle sits on top of something, like a simple logo.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain in the sense of open and obvious, not hidden, matches this word for undisguised.

clue.text: Working animals in 15's book

parts.note: working, as of a plan, means usable or functional
cats are animals

explanation.surface: Working animals feature in a book by the man of 15.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is OLD POSSUM, Eliot's nickname; his book of cat poems later became the musical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats is the poet's volume of verse about felines, so it is his book.

clue.text: Is setter on instrument in play with one performing 3's?

indicators.note: in puts the setter and instrument inside the play

parts.note: play as in amusement or fun

indicators.note: in a down entry, on places one piece above the next

parts.note: the setter is I am; asked the other way round it reads am I
a lyre is a stringed instrument
one is the Roman numeral I
on stage and performing is being on

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the compiler plays an instrument in a drama alongside an Eliot actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like the definition, Eliot's 1939 drama, but it is the container; 'Is setter' turned into a question gives the setter's 'am I'. The definition '3's' means a work of Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Family Reunion is a verse drama by T. S. Eliot, so it is a work belonging to the poet of 3.

clue.text: Ropy in relation to commotion, if inside

parts.note: re means concerning or in relation to

indicators.note: inside places the little word within the commotion

parts.note: a storm is an outburst or commotion

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something is ropy in relation to a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: This anatomical term means rope-shaped, as in the cord-like bodies of the brain stem.

clue.text: Realm of queen who has a degree?

parts.note: the queen who is a she, a female
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Asking about a monarch's kingdom, and whether the queen is a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen of Sheba visited Solomon in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical queen who visited Solomon ruled this ancient kingdom, so it is her realm.

clue.text: Skill with boat

definitions.meaning: skill as in artistry or know-how
a vessel such as a ship or boat

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a learned trade or dexterity and a vessel, as in small fishing vessels.

clue.text: Unfinished affair involving Tito with victim of Italian Fascism

indicators.note: unfinished drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: an affair is a matter, a business or issue

indicators.note: involving suggests the name is folded in and mixed

explanation.surface: An affair with Tito left incomplete, and a victim of Mussolini's Fascists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts MATTER to MATTE, and 'involving' rearranges TITO into OTTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Matteotti was the socialist deputy murdered by Fascist thugs in 1924, so he fits.

clue.text: Blazing row necessarily includes the endogenous

indicators.note: includes says the answer sits within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A blazing row inevitably includes some home-grown issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endogenous grows from within, as does a toenail that grows into the flesh.

clue.text: 3's mature marsupial breaking moulds without orders

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the broken moulds go round the orders
breaking shatters the word moulds so its letters reform

parts.note: POs are postal orders, money orders bought at a British post office

explanation.surface: An Eliot creature, an old marsupial, smashes moulds when it is not ordered to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' shuffles the moulds, and 'without' in its old sense of outside wraps them round the orders. Old Possum was Ezra Pound's nickname for Eliot; literally it is an aged marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: Old is mature and a possum is a marsupial, and the pair is the nickname Ezra Pound gave Eliot.

clue.text: Keys to much athletics: you start beyond the pale

parts.note: D is a musical key
E is another musical key

indicators.note: much of the word, its first part, is kept and the rest dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: start picks out the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Running most of the track events leaves you looking very pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' keeps ATHL of ATHLETICS, which some solvers found less than much; 'you start' gives Y. 'beyond the' joins the wordplay to the definition, deathly pale being beyond pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Deathly describes a pallor like that of a corpse, so ghastly white and wan.

clue.text: 3's work changes slightly from 31 October

indicators.note: changes slightly says two letters of the festival's name are altered

parts.note: the eve of All Saints' Day, the spooky night of trick-or-treating

explanation.surface: An Eliot poem differs only a little from the night of 31 October.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the A of HALLOWEEN to O and the second E to M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollow Men is Eliot's 1925 poem ending 'not with a bang but a whimper', so it is his work.

clue.text: Song about bounder — I was in it too

indicators.note: about places the song around the rascal

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
a cad or bounder is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A singer recalls an aria about a rogue in which they too once performed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the Latin tag Et in Arcadia ego, 'I too was in Arcadia', a saying on tombs in paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto et in Arcadia ego means 'I too was in' this pastoral paradise.

clue.text: Live among the opposition in French resort

indicators.note: among places the verb inside the opposition

parts.note: antis are those against something, the opposition
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to it chooses to live in a French seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibes is a resort town on the Côte d'Azur between Cannes and Nice.

clue.text: Beetle causing a depression in church

indicators.note: in places the depression inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a dell is a small hollow or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: A beetle causes a dip in a church floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The cadelle is a small black beetle that infests stored grain.

clue.text: Bourbon supporter giving options for motorist?

definitions.meaning: a backer of Don Carlos and his line of Spanish Bourbon claimants
read as two words, a list of cars to choose from

explanation.definitionFit: Carlists backed the Bourbon pretender Don Carlos in Spain, and a car list offers choice to drivers.

clue.text: Dummy's arrival outside strongpoint

indicators.note: outside places the newcomer around the stronghold

parts.note: a comer is one who arrives
a fort is a fortified strongpoint

explanation.surface: A dummy turns up outside a military stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: A dummy here is the British word for a baby's pacifier.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's rubber teat, given to soothe it, is also called a soother of this name in Britain.

clue.text: Use teeth to produce scream?

definitions.meaning: Edvard ... is the painter who produced The Scream

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to chew steadily, and it is the surname of the Norwegian artist of The Scream.

clue.text: Render (doctor's confession?) inaudible

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
to own is to admit or confess

explanation.surface: Making a doctor's admission impossible to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: To drown a sound is to render it inaudible; the bracketed words give the wordplay, a doctor's admission.
explanation.definitionFit: To overpower a sound with louder noise, as in shouting someone down, is to make it unheard.

clue.text: Mouth of the Dee?

parts.note: a river mouth where it splits into channels, and also the Greek letter for the sound Dee

explanation.definitionFit: A triangular river mouth takes its name from the Greek letter D, whose shape it resembles.

clue.text: Gripper to clothe pole with clothes

indicators.note: to clothe is to wrap round, so the clothes go around the pole

parts.note: togs is informal for clothes
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A gripper is used to put clothes onto a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongs are a two-armed tool for gripping coal, food or hot objects.

clue.text: Not know what will happen to one pretty girl when new line comes in

definitions.text: Not know what will happen to one

indicators.note: comes in places the reworked line inside the girl

parts.note: a bimbo is slang for an attractive but empty-headed young woman

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the word line

explanation.surface: Uncertainty for a pretty girl when a new line of text appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one pretty girl' wants to stay together, but 'one' belongs to the definition (what will happen to oneself); 'new' shuffles the line before 'comes in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state of uncertainty, awaiting an outcome, is the idiom: suspended without knowing.

clue.text: 3's called crowd to meal in hurtful surroundings

indicators.note: in places the crowd and meal inside the prickly surroundings

parts.note: thorns are hurtful, being sharp, and here form the outside
a mass is a crowd of people
tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain, joined on with to

explanation.surface: A crowd is summoned to a meal amid painful surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot's first names were Thomas Stearns, the T. S. of his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet T. S. Eliot was christened Thomas Stearns, so these are what he was called.
